posts.author: JamesdomusGames
posts.body:
I realize that I don't know really anything about making pixel art. I want to list a job offer on Fiverr for character sprite sheets for my RPG Maker game, but I don't want to underpay and I especially don't want to overpay for a couple of character sheets and side view battlers.
Can anyone give me a general range? Obviously, if an artist is in a different country, the prices could be much lower or higher given currency exchange rates, etc, but a general guideline would be very helpful.
What I'm looking for is a style similar to the RTP for a couple of enemies. Sprite sheet and side view battlers.

posts.author: JamesdomusGames
posts.body:
To be a little more specific, I'd love to know if it takes 1 hour, 10 hours or 100 hours to create a sprite sheet. Even just that would be a big help. I'm no artist, I haven't a clue how much work would go into it, so if they say $5/hour or $50/hour, but it only takes an hour, then that's better than if they want $500/hour and it takes 5 hours to make on. I have no clue.
Sorry for the double post.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: It depends on the level of detail

posts.author: Winter Witch
posts.body: You could take a look at the finished sprite sheets and tile sets that are already sold (Steam Shop, itch etc). They're usually somewhere between 10€ and 30€ (about 11USD to 35USD), depending on the amount of content. I don't know of course how much effort and how many working hours are put into them, but it might give you some insight in the average price. If you can get a tileset with A1-5 and B-E für 18$, you probably won't have to pay 100$.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Winter Witch said:
You could take a look at the finished sprite sheets and tile sets that are already sold (Steam Shop, itch etc).
Click to expand...
Those are premade assets where the creator is selling the license to use it. They can offer it cheaper since the license is sold to the masses and can be infinitely reproduced and sold. The OP wants custom made assets built to their specifications.

posts.author: JamesdomusGames
posts.body:
And character sheets for movement (which I think would be more expensive), not static tilesets, (which I think would be easier, & therefore cheaper to make).
I'm looking for something that blends nicely with the RTP style for a couple of enemies, the walking characters and then the side view battlers.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: There are plenty of sprite artists on fiverr, even specifically for RTP style. You can just go on there and see the range for yourself.
